name: City Hardwoods
old_description: In an industry filled with middlemen, our remote sawmill operation gives us the ability to supplement our wood room inventory with local hardwoods that have a unique story.
about:
City Hardwoods operates from Birmingham, Alabama, where it runs a sawmill, kiln-drying facility, and showroom The business was acquired in June 2022 by Caleb Gilbert, who runs the family-owned small business with his father. Gilbert’s path to woodworking began during his senior year at LSU when a shoulder injury sidelined him from baseball; he filled the time with weekend shop projects and soon shared the passion with his father, a lifelong hobbyist. Together they started milling and drying hardwood lumber for their own custom furniture projects.

The company’s remote sawmill salvages hundreds of urban logs each year from local tree services, diverting material that would otherwise become mulch. Logs are milled, stacked, and air-dried before finishing in one of two kilns—a dehumidification kiln and a vacuum kiln—that produce sterilized, kiln-dried lumber. Every board and slab is then surfaced on a planer or flattened on a slab CNC, a step that lets customers see grain, character, and color in the showroom. City Hardwoods builds custom furniture and retails the kiln-dried hardwood lumber, but does not offer milling or drying services to the public.

The primary customers are woodworkers, furniture buyers, and the broader Birmingham community seeking local hardwoods. The shop supplies lumber for custom furniture projects and sells boards directly to hobbyists and professionals through its retail showroom.

Gilbert says the operation was born from a desire to cut out middlemen and give each log a unique story. The dual-kiln setup ensures lumber is free of pests, and the slab CNC provides a showroom-ready surface that differentiates the buying experience. The acquisition of the existing City Hardwoods retailer in 2022 gave the family a platform to scale their sawmill output into a combined manufacturing and retail operation.

name: City Living Design Ltd
old_description: , we can help you.  Our selection of chairs, barstools, tables and lounge sofas and lounge chairs provides a variety of styles from which to choose.
about:
City Living Design Ltd operates from Chicago, Illinois, where it has supplied custom furniture for over two decades. The company traces its roots to serving restaurants and nightclubs in the Chicago area before expanding to clients across the United States. While the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the business emphasizes its long-standing presence in the contract furniture market.

The firm manufactures a range of upholstered and case goods including booths, banquettes, chairs, barstools, tables, lounge seating, and outdoor furniture. Production centers on custom fabrication: booth frames are built from kiln-dried hardwood with sinuous coil springs, webbing, and high-density foam; tabletops are offered in solid wood, butcher block, laminate, granite, glass, and stainless steel with various edge profiles. An in-house design team works with clients from concept through fabrication, and the company ships finished pieces nationwide from its Chicago workroom.

Customers span hospitality, retail, education, and corporate sectors. The company lists major department stores, national restaurant chains, upscale independent restaurants, coffee shops, diners, college campuses, and corporate employee cafes among its commercial accounts. A residential division extends the same commercial-grade construction to home kitchens, dining nooks, and living spaces, serving individual homeowners as well as interior designers and architects.

City Living Design highlights its construction methods as a differentiator—kiln-dried hardwood frames, sinuous coil springs, and high-density foam are cited for durability and ergonomic support. The firm also notes its Allied ASID membership, in-house design assistance, and the ability to deliver commercial-grade furniture for residential applications. Nationwide shipping and a collaborative quote process round out the service model.

name: City Mill - Hawaii Kai
about:
City Mill operates from Honolulu, Hawaii, where it was founded in 1899 by Chung Kun Ai. The business remains family-owned, now led by Chairman Steven C. Ai and his sister Carol Ai May, with President Shari Komo-Matsueda overseeing daily operations. The chain began as a single hardware store and has grown to eight locations across Oahu.

The company functions as a full-line hardware retailer, stocking lumber, building materials, paint, tools, plumbing, electrical, garden supplies, furniture, and housewares. In addition to retail sales, City Mill offers assembly on select items, online ordering with free in-store pickup, and local delivery from its stores. The eight locations serve the entire island of Oahu.

City Mill primarily serves Hawaii’s homeowners, DIY enthusiasts, and contractors tackling home improvement, repair, and maintenance projects. Its product assortment spans automotive and garage supplies, paint, power tools, garden and outdoor living, and native plants, reflecting the needs of the local community.

The Ai family emphasizes continuity of the service tradition established by Chung Kun Ai, focusing on knowledgeable staff and convenient shopping options tailored to island residents.

name: Clarios
old_description: Manufactures automotive batteries and energy storage systems (spun off from Johnson Controls).
about:
Clarios was founded in 2019 as a spin-off from Johnson Controls, establishing its headquarters in Glendale, Wisconsin. The company emerged as an independent entity focused on advanced battery manufacturing for the evolving transportation sector.

Today Clarios produces more than 150 million low-voltage batteries each year, employing roughly 7,000 people across a global footprint. Its product portfolio spans absorbent glass mat (AGM), lithium-ion, and supercapacitor technologies, as well as multi-battery architectures that integrate software, electronics, and AI-driven connected services. The company also develops recycled plastics for automotive applications and collaborates on sodium-ion battery industrialization.

The company serves four primary segments: automotive, commercial, powersports, and leisure. Its batteries power one in three vehicles worldwide, reaching customers in over 100 countries through brands such as LTH, MAC, Heliar, Delkor, VARTA, and OPTIMA. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket across passenger, heavy-duty, and recreational vehicles.

It differentiates itself through a chemistry-agnostic approach to low-voltage architectures, integrated electronics and software, and connected services that deliver actionable battery intelligence. Recent initiatives include expanding recycled plastics content and advancing sodium-ion technology with partners Altris and InoBat.

name: Clark Truck Equipment Company Inc.
old_description: SERVING NEW MEXICO WITH QUALITY TRUCK EQUIPMENT FOR OVER 75 YEARS
about:
Clark Truck Equipment Company Inc. operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it has served the Southwest since 1964. The business traces its roots to 1947 when Morris H. Clark opened a Winter‑Weiss Company branch in a former lettuce‑processing shed. Clark’s sons, Chuck and Don, grew up in the shop, and in 1964 the family acquired controlling interest to form Clark Truck Equipment Co. The company remains family‑owned today.

The company functions as a dealer and full‑service provider for specialized truck equipment, offering aerial lifts, flatbeds, cranes, refuse bodies, water trucks and related aftermarket parts. Beyond sales, it provides professional installation, repair, fleet maintenance, inspections, frame modifications, trailer repairs and custom fabrication. Its current 24,000‑square‑foot facility on 6.5 fenced acres includes 14 drive‑through bays equipped with welders, torches and a stand‑alone paint booth, and carries an inventory valued at over $750,000.

Customers span commercial, governmental and retail sectors across New Mexico and the broader Southwest. Notable accounts include the City of Albuquerque, Public Service Company of New Mexico, Kirtland Air Force Base, Navajo Utility Authority and various mining operations, alongside individual owner‑operators.

Clark Truck Equipment emphasizes its multi‑generational expertise, long‑tenured workforce (with employees marking 25‑ and 40‑year careers), and membership in the National Truck Equipment Association since 1967 as the foundation of its reputation for quality and personalized service.

name: ClassOne Technology
old_description: Electroplating and Wet Processing for Advanced Microelectronics
about:
ClassOne Technology is headquartered in Kalispell, Montana, where it designs and manufactures electroplating and wet‑processing equipment for advanced microelectronics. The company operates as ClassOne Technology Inc. and serves the semiconductor industry from its facility No founding year or founders are disclosed.

The company’s product line centers on the Solstice platform, offered in two configurations: the Solstice Max for 200 mm and 300 mm wafers (2–16 chambers) and the Solstice S‑Series for 3‑inch to 200 mm wafers (2–8 chambers). Both platforms are modular and field‑extendable. The equipment portfolio includes dedicated process chambers: the GoldPro™ Chamber, CopperMax™ Chamber, and Gen4 ECD Chamber for electroplating; a Wet Etch Chamber; and a Solvent & MLO Chamber for surface preparation. These chambers support a range of processes — copper TSV fill, copper RDL and pillar plating, multi‑metal stack pillars, advanced gold plating (including TWV, patterned, deplating, and fine‑feature fill), photoresist strip, metal lift‑off, UBM and patterned metal wet etch, RCA cleans (SC1/SC2), piranha (SPM), and emerging applications such as through‑glass vias, indium bump plating, and hybrid bonding.

ClassOne’s systems target advanced packaging houses, RF and sensor manufacturers, high‑reliability device makers, photonics and advanced‑sensor developers, and compound‑ and power‑semiconductor fabs. The company positions its tools for both production and R&D environments, emphasizing flexibility across a broad set of backend applications.

ClassOne states that its differentiator lies in removing “unnecessary complexity common to competitors” in favor of “more elegant and intuitive designs,” which it says yields faster recipe dial‑in, longer uptime, and lower operator and engineering burden. The platform is described as a common, easy‑to‑use, high‑performance foundation that maximizes performance relative to complexity and cost.

name: Cleantap Energy
old_description: Cleantap Energy, LLC is an energetic Maine based solar project development company with a team bringing decades of experience.
about:
Based in Gray, Maine, Cleantap Energy, LLC operates as a solar project development and installation company. The firm describes itself as a Maine-based team with decades of combined experience in the solar industry.

The company designs and installs custom photovoltaic systems for residential and commercial customers, including retrofit solutions for existing properties. Its services span site evaluation, system design, permitting, installation, and assistance with incentive paperwork such as the 30% federal tax credit and USDA REAP grants. According to its website, the team has completed 84 renewable energy projects, assisted 62 businesses with renewable transitions, and maintains 16 installation crews.

Cleantap Energy serves homeowners throughout Maine seeking to reduce electricity costs, as well as businesses ranging from small commercial operations to larger facilities that can leverage accelerated depreciation and grant programs. The company also works with agricultural clients, noting that systems can be built on existing farms or ranches.

The firm emphasizes a transparent, customer-focused approach, promising to remove the guesswork from solar adoption. It highlights its local presence, warranty responsiveness—such as replacing a faulty panel within days—and a commitment to sustainability as key differentiators.

name: ClearLake Furniture
old_description: Need inspiration on how to style your dream room? ClearLake Furniture offers exclusive Interior Design Services to help you boldly furnish your Vermont home.
about:
ClearLake Furniture was founded in 1992 by master woodworker Brent Karner in Ludlow, Vermont. The company operates from a beautifully restored barn in Windsor County, where a 3,000-square-foot gallery showcases custom hardwood pieces alongside the active workshop.

The shop produces made-to-order furniture including dining tables, seating, cabinetry, beds, and limited-edition collections, along with commercial furnishings and kitchen remodels. Each piece is built by a single craftsman using traditional joinery—interlocking joints, splined miters, and dovetails—and finished in-house. The team of nine craftsmen and staff also provides interior design services, virtual consultations, a gift registry, and a trade-in program that credits older pieces toward new work.

Clients range from Vermont homeowners furnishing primary residences and wedding registries to commercial accounts such as Ludlow Medical Center. The design studio works directly with customers to select style, dimensions, wood species, and finish, even inviting them to choose the actual boards from the lumber stacks.

Karner’s original commitment to detail and personal involvement remains the guiding principle: every item is signed and dated by its maker with the client’s family name, backed by the ClearLake Guarantee, and eligible for the Investment Program that allows future trade-ins.

name: Cleaveland/Price Inc
old_description: Cleaveland/Price offers a wide array of switch products. Choose the switch product(s) that best suits your company needs.
about:
Cleaveland/Price Inc. traces its origins to 1975 in Trafford, Pennsylvania, when Chuck Cleaveland took on the responsibility of supplying renewal parts for discontinued Westinghouse switches. Operating initially as a renewal parts supplier, the company's engineers began developing their own switch designs to address shortcomings they observed in existing products.

Today the company manufactures a full line of group-operated switches rated up to 345 kV, hookstick-operated switches, and motor operators. Its product portfolio also includes transmission-class in-line disconnect switches, solid-state motor operator controls, variable-speed motor operators, non-hydraulic operators for overhead switches, and automation controllers for retrofitting padmount and underground switchgear. Additional offerings encompass line sensors and data collectors such as the LineScope™ Power Quality Monitor, Reliatronics RTUs, and StayDry® corrosion-resistant bearing assemblies with hydrophobic membrane technology. Production takes place in a vertically integrated facility with extensive CNC machining capabilities.

Cleaveland/Price serves the medium- and high-voltage electrical industry, supplying utilities, switchgear manufacturers, and automation integrators. Its automation products, including DNP 3.0 certified controllers, target retrofits of padmount and underground switchgear, while its line sensors and RTUs support power quality monitoring and data acquisition for grid operations.

The company attributes its growth to a continuous R&D program and a vertically integrated manufacturing model that allows rapid iteration. Founder Chuck Cleaveland's stated goal of "no unhappy customers" underpins a quality policy emphasizing on-time, defect-free delivery and ethical dealings, with a certificate of registration available upon request.

about:
Cleveland Creek Home Furnishings operates from Broomfield, Colorado, with a warehouse in Golden and three retail showrooms in Golden, Boulder, and Lakewood. The company has been producing custom furniture for nearly two decades and is owned by Geoff Cleveland, who runs it as a locally owned, family-operated small business.

The shop specializes in custom handmade wood furniture and home accessories, covering bedroom, dining, living room, and office categories. Each piece is built to order using various wood species that the company says are locally and responsibly sourced. Production takes place at the Golden warehouse, while the showrooms display a fraction of the available designs; pricing varies by style and wood selection.

The primary customers are residential buyers, interior designers, and homeowners seeking one-of-a-kind pieces for private homes. The product line includes beds, dining tables, living room seating, and office furniture, all positioned as heirloom-quality items meant to last lifetimes.

The company states its mission is to provide furniture that is second to none, sourced and constructed in the most conscientious and responsible ways. Its vision ties continued growth to a focus on quality and customer satisfaction, with the goal of reinvesting in a expanding home accessory gallery.
